> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **13** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2b1382a5b3887e4abd194411ef77a7cd368c95c2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d7f4667d1dbe9a8c17925d88d2ddd074aa449962` — the merge of head `cc15060f7e5bb2ff2e1efc905688bc9f0dc83362` into base `2b1382a5b3887e4abd194411ef77a7cd368c95c2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d7f4667d1dbe9a8c17925d88d2ddd074aa449962 && git checkout d7f4667d1dbe9a8c17925d88d2ddd074aa449962
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2b1382a5b3887e4abd194411ef77a7cd368c95c2 cc15060f7e5bb2ff2e1efc905688bc9f0dc83362 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2b1382a5b3887e4abd194411ef77a7cd368c95c2 && git merge --no-ff cc15060f7e5bb2ff2e1efc905688bc9f0dc83362

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2b1382a5b3887e4abd194411ef77a7cd368c95c2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2b1382a5b3887e4abd194411ef77a7cd368c95c2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `cc15060f7e5bb2ff2e1efc905688bc9f0dc83362`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sqlite-database-file.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-25019-sqlite-damaged-file-and-dangling-link.test.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/sqlite-driver-fallback.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/__tests__/sqlite-driver-fallback-damaged-file-and-dangling-link.test.ts + packages/drivers/driver-sqlite-wasm/src/wasm-connection.ts (open, assertReadable, quarantineCorruptFile), packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-connection-service.ts (connect, handleFailure), packages/services/service-datasource/src/default-datasource-driver-factory.ts (the sqlite and sqlite-wasm arms), packages/services/service-datasource/src/connect-failure-remedy.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/db/clean.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/telemetry-datasource.ts, packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/turso-driver.ts (connect, disconnect), examples/app-showcase/src/system/datasources/external-fixture.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/index.ts (the export surface), scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs (the launch-window convention), .changeset/25019-sqlite-file-failure-family.md (the prose face, read for ②)

Inputs: card #25019 (its body and comments 6305577138, 6305864303, 6307297304, 6310958104, 6311031589); PR #25006 and PR #25007 (bodies) with their contract-review records 6305645762 and 6305566864; PR #25080 (body, 6-file list, and the net diff `origin/main...cc15060f7` read locally: merge base `157ebd008`, the same 6 files, +644/-13); the check-runs on the head, read ONCE, after the second suite's 07:59:01Z start, and not polled. Read-only throughout: nothing built, run or re-run; no worktree. `sql-driver.ts` was read at the head in the regions the hunks cite (connect, applyAutoVacuumIncremental, SQLITE_FILE_REFUSALS, ensureDatabaseExists, sqliteFilename, resolveSqliteAbsentFileTarget, knexConfigFor). The dispatch order and the dispatching seat's other conclusions were not inputs.

**Check-runs on the head, exactly as read (48 runs):** 38 `success`, 9 `skipped`, 1 `in_progress`, 0 failed. Green: Build Core; Test Core (the aggregate and shards 1/6 to 6/6); TypeScript Type Check with Type Check workspace, consumer gates, source gates and debt ledger; Lint & Repo Gates with Lint ESLint, CI release & engine gates, docs & code guards, repo & tooling gates, PM dispatch-gates and the three scoped lanes; Governed Surface Queue Guard; Dogfood Regression Gate (the unsharded run); Check Documentation Links; Flag docs affected by code changes; filter; Check PR Size and Auto Label (first suite); and the four claim guards (No other open PR may claim the same issue, No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path, Part-of PR must not also close its card, The card this PR closes must claim this branch) in both suites. `skipped`: 18.x upgrade harness, Packed-tarball smoke, Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, the sharded Dogfood Regression Gate, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance, and the second suite's Check PR Size and Auto Label. `Check Changeset` ran twice on this head: run 119094153764 (suite 107209126144, completed 07:25:20Z) is `success`; run 119107814416 (suite 107220315424, started 07:59:01Z after the PR body edit) is `in_progress` with no conclusion yet. The queue is armed on that second run's own verdict, not on this record.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong:

1. **`SqlDriver.connect()` accept set, minus `SQLITE_CORRUPT` at the first statement: right.** `SQLITE_FILE_REFUSALS` grows from two rows to three; the lookup, the `SqliteDatabaseFileError(filename, words, cause)` throw and every other branch of `applyAutoVacuumIncremental`'s catch are unchanged (native-load failures still warn the one-liner and return `false`; anything else keeps the full warning and `false`). The refusal is raised before `applySqliteJournalMode` and before any write. Only SQLite clients reach it (`connect()` gates on `isSqlite`); `:memory:` and the `openedEmptyInMemory` redirect never answer this code.
2. **`SqlDriver.connect()` accept set, minus a directory level a dangling symbolic link holds: right.** `makeDatabaseDirectory`'s upward walk now asks `isDanglingLink(level)` at each level `stat` answers `ENOENT` for, and throws `danglingLinkRefusal(level, e)`, a plain `Error` carrying `stat`'s `code` (`ENOENT`) and `cause`, before the level joins `missing`. `ensureDatabaseExists` wraps it as it wrapped every walk failure, so the surface is `SqliteDatabaseFileError`, `code: 'ENOENT'`, message `SQLite database file 'F' cannot be created: its directory 'D' could not be made: 'LINK' is a symbolic link to a path that does not exist: ENOENT ...`. Before, `mkdir` answered `EEXIST` on the link, the creating loop took that for a concurrent creator, and better-sqlite3's code-less `TypeError` was swallowed: the connect resolved over a datasource no statement could use. Nothing that worked stops working.
3. **`resolveSqliteAbsentFileTarget` (a value export of `@objectstack/driver-sql`), the `SqlDriver` constructor under `sqliteAbsentFile: 'empty-in-memory'`, and the service's `wasmFilename` line: accept set minus a dangling link as the FILE whose chain ends in a directory that does not exist or does not allow write and search: right, and declared.** `probeAbsentSqliteDatabaseFile` runs `danglingLinkEnd` only after `stat(filename)` answered `ENOENT`; a non-link returns `undefined` on hop 0 and the directory walk runs as before. The dev's claim allowed "pin it or name it out of scope"; the dev fixed it on the claim's own file, pinned it (two cases, direct and through a second link, with controls for an existing target directory, absolute and relative targets) and ablated it (leg 4). The changeset's third bullet, its BREAKING banner and the PR body's narrowing paragraph all name it. This is the family note 6305577138's shape, closed.
4. **`resolveSqliteDriver`'s development step-down, minus `SQLITE_CORRUPT`: right.** `isSqliteFileOpenFailure` is still judged on `code` alone, no message text; the dangling-link refusals carry `ENOENT`, which the `^E[A-Z0-9]+$` arm already classified, so member 2 needed no line here (pinned: the development resolve over the link rejects with no warning and no wasm rung). Production is untouched (native unprobed; the refusal comes from the service's `handle.connect()`). The native-load step-down keeps its path: the control with a real `ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED` over a real database still reaches wasm, warns `NATIVE_SQLITE_WASM_FALLBACK_WARNING`, reads the rows and renames nothing.
5. **`SqliteDatabaseFileError`: the code set gains `SQLITE_CORRUPT` and one more producer of `ENOENT`; the shape (`name`, `code`, `filename`, `cause`, the message form) is unchanged.** `src/index.ts` still exports `resolveSqliteAbsentFileTarget` alone from this pair; the class, `makeDatabaseDirectory`, `probeAbsentSqliteDatabaseFile` and the three new helpers (`danglingLinkWords`, `danglingLinkRefusal`, `danglingLinkEnd`) are package-private. No published declaration moved; the PR's "Nothing exported changes shape" holds.
6. **The wasm quarantine is unchanged, by the diff.** `git diff origin/main...cc15060f7 -- packages/drivers/driver-sqlite-wasm` is empty. At the head, `WasmSqliteConnection.open()` still reads the bytes, `new SQL.Database(bytes)` or `assertReadable`'s `PRAGMA quick_check(1)` throws, and `quarantineCorruptFile` renames to `FILE.corrupt-TIMESTAMP` and starts an empty database, in every mode. What still reaches it is exactly the seat's ruled member 3: the development step-down with an addon that cannot load, and a datasource declared `driver: 'sqlite-wasm'` (the factory's `sqlite-wasm` arm builds `SqliteWasmDriver` directly). This PR adds no door to it and closes the two the card named.

**(a) Classifying `SQLITE_CORRUPT` as a whole-file refusal: right.** The first statement is the READ `PRAGMA auto_vacuum` (`applyAutoVacuumIncremental`; knex's better-sqlite3 client runs nothing on acquire and the driver installs no sqlite `afterCreate`). In SQLite's own pragma table `auto_vacuum` carries the NeedSchema flag, so that read forces the full schema load: page 1's header (a bad magic string is `SQLITE_NOTADB`; a header page count beyond the file is `SQLITE_CORRUPT`) and then every `sqlite_schema` row, whose b-tree pages must read and whose CREATE text must parse (`corruptSchema` answers `SQLITE_CORRUPT`, "malformed database schema"). A `SQLITE_CORRUPT` there is the answer every statement that names a table repeats, because each re-attempts the same load; the dev measured `SELECT 1` answering the same code on every shape in the table (truncation at 50..4095 bytes, to one page, to half the pages, a garbled schema b-tree, a page count larger than the file). So nothing ObjectStack does on such a datasource could succeed, and refusing it turns away no working datasource. Damage below the schema (a table or index page, the freelist) loads the schema and connects, and surfaces on the read or write that reaches it; the dev's CONTROL pins that shape (the table's root page overwritten; connect resolves; the read fails with `SQLITE_CORRUPT` as its cause). Two shapes, by code reading and not measured, answer `SQLITE_CORRUPT` at the first statement with intact bytes, and neither is a working datasource: a schema written with syntax this SQLite build cannot parse (a file from a newer SQLite, for instance a STRICT table on an older engine; `corruptSchema` names it "malformed database schema (NAME) - ..." and the refusal carries that cause text, so the operator can tell), and a foreign or stale `-wal` beside a healthy main file (the refusal names the main file alone). For both, the words "is damaged" are loose, the effect is right, and before this PR a development boot renamed the file. One line on the mechanism: the `catch` wraps the setter `PRAGMA auto_vacuum = INCREMENTAL` as well as the read; the setter runs only when the read answered and touches page 1 alone (a FULL-to-INCREMENTAL switch skips compaction; a NONE file with pages is a silent no-op in SQLite), so in practice the verdict is the first statement's. Extended codes: better-sqlite3 reports `sqlite3_extended_errcode`, and the lookup is an exact string; `SQLITE_CORRUPT_VTAB`, `_SEQUENCE` and `_INDEX` arise at vtab connect, autoincrement and integrity_check, none of which a schema load runs, and the dev measured none at the first statement.

**(b) The dangling-link refusals: right.** Directory: the writing boot refuses exactly the levels the read-only boot refuses (the same upward walk from `dirname(resolve(filename))`, the same `isDanglingLink` test, which is `lstat` succeeding where `stat` answered `ENOENT`, which only a dangling link does), with the same class, the same code (`stat`'s `ENOENT` on both) and the same link words through `danglingLinkWords`; the outer verbs differ by one word ("could not be made" on the writing boot, "cannot be made" on the read-only one), which predates this PR for every shape (#23696, #24961), and the pins assert class, `code`, `filename` and the link words on both boots at both depths. File: the read-only boot now refuses what the writing boot already refused with SQLite's own `SQLITE_CANTOPEN`; the codes differ (`ENOENT`, the target's directory named, against SQLite's answer that names the file) as `ENOTDIR` against `EEXIST` already did on #24961, each the system's own answer; pinned side by side. Bound: `danglingLinkEnd` runs only after `stat` answered `ENOENT`, so the kernel has already resolved the chain to an end within its own 40-link limit (a cycle answers `ELOOP`, refused one branch earlier as "cannot be opened or created"); the loop's bound of at most 40 hops restates that, and any `readlink` or `realpath` failure ends the walk at the current name. Relative targets: each hop is `resolve(realpathSync(dirname(at)), readlinkSync(at))`, the real directory of the link that holds it, as the kernel reads it; a hop whose directory is itself missing or a dangling link ends the chain there, and `where` then fails `stat` and is refused as "does not exist". Writes: `danglingLinkEnd`, `statSync(where)` and `accessSync(where, W_OK | X_OK)` write nothing; the writing walk throws before the level joins `missing`, so its creating loop never runs; both pins assert the directory listing unchanged and the link still dangling. `where` is a directory whenever it exists, because a regular file on the chain answers `stat(filename)` with `ENOTDIR`, refused earlier.

**(c) Every caller whose answer flips: no FAIL item.** No caller crashes, swallows a refusal into success, or renames or replaces an operator's file. The census: outside tests the tree holds no direct `new SqlDriver({ client: 'better-sqlite3' })`; every sqlite construction goes through `resolveSqliteDriver` (four callers) or `DatasourceConnectionService`.
   - `DatasourceConnectionService.connect` / `connectDeclared`, through the factory's `sqlite` arm (development: the resolver closes its probe and re-throws; production: native unprobed, `handle.connect()` rejects inside the service's `try`): `handleFailure` records `failed-degraded` and warns "degrading (datasource left unconnected)" when nothing binds, and throws the fail-fast line naming the file when an object binds, a mapping routes, or the host declared it boot-critical (ADR-0062 D5; `OS_ALLOW_DRIVER_CONNECT_FAILURE` degrades instead). New answers: a header- or schema-damaged file, both modes (before: production resolved and the first query failed; development renamed it through wasm and read connected); a dangling-link directory, both modes and both factories (before: resolved, then a code-less failure, or the wasm rung). The primary `default` datasource is boot-critical, so `os dev` over a damaged `.objectstack/data` file now refuses the boot naming the file instead of renaming it and starting empty: the card's own ⛔ line, and the cost the seat's ruling names. Pinned in both modes, no driver registered, nothing moved aside. Right.
   - `os db clean` (`dev: true`, the primary and the telemetry sibling): the refusal is caught per target, printed as `VACUUM failed for FILE: ...`, and the command exits 1; before, a damaged primary was quarantined by wasm and the empty replacement VACUUMed and reported compact. Right.
   - `provisionTelemetryDatasource` (the development telemetry sibling): the `catch` answers `undefined`, so a damaged sibling file is neither renamed nor reported and lifecycle-classed objects stay on the primary. Pre-existing best-effort shape, named by family note 6305864303, ⛔ out of the claim; the PR names it. Right as scoped (③ item 3).
   - `TursoDriver.connect()` local and replica: `super.connect()` runs first, before any libsql client or sync, with no catch; a local or replica file SQLite cannot read is refused at connect naming the file. Before, connect resolved and every read, all of which run through the inherited Knex engine, failed with the same code; a replica's `sync()` cannot read a damaged local file either. No working datasource flips. By code reading; the claim ⛔s the turso driver and the diff holds no turso pin. Right.
   - `setupShowcaseExternalDatasource` (examples/app-showcase): `resolveSqliteDriver` with `dev` from `NODE_ENV` on the fixture file; a damaged fixture now rejects `onEnable` naming the file (development: re-thrown by the resolver; production: `fixture.connect()` throws, uncaught). Before, development renamed and re-provisioned it. Not in the dev's caller list (the same omission 6305645762 noted); the card's ⛔ applied to a declared fixture. Right.
   - The read-only boots (`sqliteAbsentFile: 'empty-in-memory'`): a damaged file that exists is opened and refused at the first statement like any boot; the dangling file link is item 3; the dangling-link directory was already refused (#24961). Right.
   - `driver: 'sqlite-wasm'` declared: unchanged, member 3.

**(d) The refusal envelope: right.** Each refusal is `SqliteDatabaseFileError` with `filename` the declared path, `code` the cause's own (`SQLITE_CORRUPT`; `ENOENT`), `cause` the error itself, and the message `SQLite database file 'F' WORDS: CAUSE` naming the file, the link (directory member) or the chain's end and its directory (file member). It echoes nothing secret: a sqlite connection carries no credential, the messages carry paths and SQLite's or the operating system's own text, and `TursoDriver`'s `encryptionKey` is not on the path. PR #25006's shape is kept to the constructor. The driver-sql pins assert `toBeInstanceOf(SqliteDatabaseFileError)`, `code`, `filename`, the file in the message and the cause's message inside it; the service pins assert `name === 'SqliteDatabaseFileError'`, `code`, `filename` and the file in the message (duck-typed, as the class is not published), plus the link words and the chain's target where they apply; `connectDeclared`'s `reason` is asserted to carry the file and the link.

7. Pin hygiene: both new files read their own `mkdtemp` scratch alone (`check:cross-package-test-inputs` not implicated); the service pin's unaliased `@objectstack/driver-sql` import is the registered `KNOWN_UNALIASED_TEST_IMPORTS` pair; both sit outside `files[]`; `tsc --listFiles` reaches each (the dev's reading; CI's type-check lanes are green). The ablation's four legs each turned the predicted pins red and nothing else, with restore proven; read, not re-run.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no (narrowing)

- **Declaration.** `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and in `.changeset/25019-sqlite-file-failure-family.md`; nothing authorable is added, and the arm the diff publishes is a narrowing on three fronts: `SqlDriver.connect()` over a damaged file and over a dangling-link directory, and the read-only judgement over a dangling file link. Right.
- **Level.** `@objectstack/driver-sql: minor`, `@objectstack/service-datasource: minor`. Right: both packages move published source (`sql-driver.ts` and `sqlite-database-file.ts`; `sqlite-driver-fallback.ts`), a declared narrowing is BREAKING, and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` ships a breaking change as `minor` during the launch window with the banner and the ADR-0087 disposition as its carriers; its level axis refuses `patch` on a moved package under this declaration. `Check Changeset` is `success` on this head in its first run; the second run is in progress as read.
- **BREAKING banner and migration.** Present, with Before / Now / Fix; the Fix is the operator's (restore or move the damaged file aside, an absent file is created empty; re-point the link or the datasource), which is all a consumer needs: no declaration, spec key, config field or stored shape moves.
- **ADR-0087 disposition.** `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` with the other categories closed on facts. Right: `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to rewrite and the body carries no consumer-code prescription. One loose clause inside the marker, prose only: "no exported declaration is ... narrowed" sits beside a narrowing of `resolveSqliteAbsentFileTarget`'s accept set (① item 3), which the changeset's own third bullet and banner declare; the disposition does not turn on it.
- **Prose.** The PR body's "What changed" says `minor` for both packages, matching the changeset. The changeset heading carries no conventional bang, as the family's two landed siblings did not; the banner and the `Clause-②` line carry the breaking-ness and no gate reads the bang. The `SqliteDatabaseFileError` class doc still names only #23696 and #24960 and lists codes without `SQLITE_CORRUPT`: doc-only residue, not a contract matter; a push to fix it would move the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every dev deviation and out-of-scope finding in 6310958104, answered or escalated; the member-3 fork is answered by the seat's ruling 6311031589.

1. **Member 3 against the ruling: agrees.** The ruling binds route A to a later PR (wasm refuses, `quarantineCorruptFile` retires, `resolveSqliteDriver` re-throws a wasm file refusal, `driver-sqlite-wasm` and `service-datasource` at `minor`), serial after this PR because both edit `sqlite-driver-fallback.ts`, and orders this PR to `Part of #25019`. PR #25080's first line is `Part of #25019`, its second paragraph states the ruling and that the merge does not close the card, the `Part-of PR must not also close its card` and `The card this PR closes must claim this branch` guards are `success` in both suites on this head, and the diff holds no line of `driver-sqlite-wasm` and no wasm re-throw in `isSqliteFileOpenFailure` or the wasm rung: nothing here pre-empts or contradicts what the ruling binds. The dev report's note that the PR carried `Fixes` is superseded by the switch.
2. **Out-of-scope finding 1 (carrier: none), a refused connect's pool stays open on the production path: ESCALATED to the seat, not a FAIL item.** Read in the cited code: `DatasourceConnectionService.connect` catches the `handle.connect()` rejection, unregisters only what this attempt registered, and calls `handleFailure`; it never calls `handle.disconnect()`, and `SqlDriver.connect()` does not destroy its Knex pool on a refusal, whose one better-sqlite3 handle the pool keeps. For a damaged file whose header says WAL, SQLite then keeps `-shm` and an empty `-wal` beside it for the process's life (the development resolver closes its probe, pinned: the directory holds the file alone). The operator's bytes are untouched, the sidecars are SQLite's own and go at close, the same open handle predates this PR for `SQLITE_CANTOPEN` and `SQLITE_NOTADB`, and on the fail-fast path the process exits. Prime Directive 10 wants it filed: a reproducible defect with a measured mechanism and dedupe words already on the card.
